units.Malachi 1:1: A pronouncement of the word of the Lord concerning Israel through His messenger. Take it to your hearts!
units.Malachi 1:2: “I have loved you,” says the Lord. But you said, “How hast Thou loved us?” “Was not Esau Jacob’s brother?” says the Lord. “Yet I loved Jacob,
units.Malachi 1:3: but Esau I hated. I appointed his territories for desolation and his inheritance as gifts of a wilderness.”
units.Malachi 1:4: Because Idumea will say, “It has been overthrown; let us return and rebuild the deserted places,” thus says the Lord Almighty: “They will build, but I will overthrow. They will be called ‘Territories of Lawlessness’ and ‘A People Against Whom the Lord Has Drawn Up His Forces Forever.’”
units.Malachi 1:5: Your eyes will see, and you yourselves will say, “The Lord has been magnified beyond Israel’s territories!”
units.Malachi 1:6: “A son honors his father, and a slave his master. If I am a father, where is My honor? If I am a master, where is the fear of Me?” says the Lord Almighty. You priests who belittle My name! But you said, “How have we belittled Thy name?”
units.Malachi 1:7: “By bringing polluted loaves to My altar.” But you said, “How have we polluted them?” “By your saying, ‘The Lord’s table is despised, and the foods placed upon it are despised.’”
units.Malachi 1:8: “For if you bring a blind animal for sacrifice, is that not evil? If you bring one that is lame or sick, is that not evil? Bring it, then, to your ruler! Will he accept it? Will he show you favor?” says the Lord Almighty.
units.Malachi 1:9: “And now appease the face of your God and plead with Him. These things have happened in your hands. Will I show favor to any of you?” says the Lord Almighty.
units.Malachi 1:10: “For even among you doors will be shut, and you will not kindle My altar for nothing. I have no desire for you,” says the Lord Almighty, “and I will not accept a sacrifice from your hands.”
units.Malachi 1:11: “For from the sun’s rising to its setting, My name has been glorified among the nations, and in every place incense is brought to My name, together with a pure sacrifice, because My name is great among the nations,” says the Lord Almighty.
units.Malachi 1:12: “But you profane it by your saying, ‘The Lord’s table is polluted, and the foods placed upon it are despised.’
units.Malachi 1:13: “And you said, ‘These things are from hardship,’ and I blew them away,” says the Lord Almighty. “You were bringing things seized by force, the lame and the afflicted. If you bring the sacrifice, shall I accept these things from your hands?” says the Lord Almighty.
units.Malachi 1:14: “Cursed is one who was able, and had a male in his flock and a vow concerning it, yet sacrifices a damaged animal to the Lord. For I am a great King,” says the Lord Almighty, “and My name is manifest among the nations.”
units.Malachi 2:1: “And now this command is for you, priests.
units.Malachi 2:2: If you do not listen and do not take it into your hearts to give glory to My name,” says the Lord Almighty, “I will send out the curse upon you, and I will curse your blessing, and I will curse it. I will scatter your blessing, and it will not be among you, because you do not take it into your hearts.
units.Malachi 2:3: Look, I am setting apart the shoulder for you, and I will scatter the stomach on your faces, the stomach of your festivals, and I will take you to the same place.
units.Malachi 2:4: You will recognize that I have sent out this command to you, so that My covenant might be with the Levites,” says the Lord Almighty.
units.Malachi 2:5: “My covenant with him was of life and peace, and I gave it to him in fear, to fear Me and to shrink back before My name.
units.Malachi 2:6: A law of truth was in his mouth, and injustice was not found on his lips. Directing his way in peace, he walked with Me and turned many back from injustice.
units.Malachi 2:7: For a priest’s lips will guard knowledge, and people will seek law from his mouth, because he is the messenger of the Lord Almighty.
units.Malachi 2:8: But you have turned aside from the way and weakened many through the law; you have corrupted the covenant of Levi,” says the Lord Almighty.
units.Malachi 2:9: “And I have made you despised and neglected among all the nations, because you did not guard My ways but showed partiality in the law.”
units.Malachi 2:10: Did not one God create you? Is there not one Father of you all? Why have you each abandoned your brother, so as to profane the covenant of your fathers?
units.Malachi 2:11: Judah has been abandoned, and an abomination has occurred in Israel and Jerusalem, because Judah profaned the Lord’s holy things, in which he delighted, and devoted himself to foreign gods.
units.Malachi 2:12: The Lord will destroy the person who does these things, until he is also humbled away from Jacob’s dwellings and from those who bring a sacrifice to the Lord Almighty.
units.Malachi 2:13: And you were doing these things that I hated: you covered the Lord’s altar with tears, with weeping and groaning from hardships. Is it still fitting to look toward a sacrifice or accept it from your hands?
units.Malachi 2:14: And you said, “For what reason?” Because the Lord bore witness between you and the wife of your youth, whom you abandoned, though she is your partner and the wife of your covenant.
units.Malachi 2:15: And no other did it, and there was a remnant of his spirit. And you said, “What else does God seek but offspring?” So guard your spirit, and do not abandon the wife of your youth.
units.Malachi 2:16: But if, after hating her, you send her away, says the Lord, the God of Israel, impiety will cover your thoughts, says the Lord Almighty. So guard your spirit, and you must not abandon.
units.Malachi 2:17: You who provoke God with your words! And you said, “How have we provoked Him?” By your saying, “Everyone who does evil is good before the Lord, and He has delighted in them,” and, “Where is the God of righteousness?”
units.Malachi 3:1: “Look, I am sending out My messenger, and he will look to a way before My face. Suddenly the Lord whom you seek will come to His own sanctuary, and the messenger of the covenant whom you desire. Look, he is coming,” says the Lord Almighty.
units.Malachi 3:2: And who will endure the day of his entrance? Or who will stand at his appearance? For he enters like a smelting fire and like launderers’ herb.
units.Malachi 3:3: He will sit, smelting and purifying as with silver and gold. He will cleanse the sons of Levi and melt them like gold and silver, and they will be those who bring a sacrifice to the Lord in righteousness.
units.Malachi 3:4: And the sacrifice of Judah and Jerusalem will please the Lord, as in the days of old and as in the former years.
units.Malachi 3:5: “I will draw near to you in judgment, and I will be a swift witness against sorceresses, adulteresses and those who swear falsely by My name, against those who withhold a hired worker’s wages, those who oppress a widow, those who strike orphans with their fists, those who turn aside the judgment of a sojourner, and those who do not fear Me,” says the Lord Almighty.
units.Malachi 3:6: “For I am the Lord your God, and I have not changed. But you, sons of Jacob, do not refrain
units.Malachi 3:7: from the injustices of your fathers. You have turned aside from My ordinances and have not guarded them. Return to Me, and I will return to you,” says the Lord Almighty. And you said, “How shall we return?”
units.Malachi 3:8: “Will a human defraud God? Yet you are defrauding Me.” And you will say, “How have we defrauded Thee?” “Because the tithes and the firstfruits are with you.
units.Malachi 3:9: And you keep looking away, yet you are defrauding Me. The nation has been brought to an end.
units.Malachi 3:10: And you brought all the produce dues into the storehouses, and his plunder will be in his house. Examine, then, by this,” says the Lord Almighty, “whether I will not open heaven’s floodgates for you and pour out My blessing for you until there is enough.
units.Malachi 3:11: And I will give you instructions for food, and I will certainly not destroy the fruit of your land, and your vine in the field will certainly not grow weak,” says the Lord Almighty.
units.Malachi 3:12: “All the nations will call you blessed, because you will be a desirable land,” says the Lord Almighty.
units.Malachi 3:13: “You have made your words heavy against Me,” says the Lord. And you said, “How have we spoken against Thee?”
units.Malachi 3:14: You said, “The one who serves God is futile. What advantage is there because we guarded His observances and because we walked as supplicants before the Lord Almighty?
units.Malachi 3:15: And now we call outsiders blessed. All who practice lawlessness are being built up; they opposed God and were saved.”
units.Malachi 3:16: Those who feared the Lord spoke these things, each to his neighbor. The Lord paid attention and listened, and He wrote a book of remembrance before Him for those who feared the Lord and revered His name.
units.Malachi 3:17: “They will be Mine,” says the Lord Almighty, “for a day that I am making for an acquisition, and I will choose them as a man chooses his son who serves him.
units.Malachi 3:18: And you will return and see the distinction between the righteous and the lawless, and between one who serves God and one who does not serve.
units.Malachi 3:19: For look, the day of the Lord is coming, burning like an oven, and it will burn them. All the foreigners and all who practice lawlessness will be straw, and the coming day will ignite them,” says the Lord Almighty, “and neither root nor branch will remain from them.
units.Malachi 3:20: But for you who fear My name, a sun of righteousness will rise, and healing in its wings; you will go out and leap like little calves released from bonds.
units.Malachi 3:21: You will trample the lawless, because they will be ashes beneath your feet on the day that I am making,” says the Lord Almighty.
units.Malachi 3:22: “And look, I am sending you Elijah the Tishbite before the coming of the Lord’s great and manifest day,
units.Malachi 3:23: who will restore a father’s heart toward a son and a person’s heart toward his neighbor, lest I come and strike the land utterly.”
units.Malachi 3:24: “All of you, remember the law of Moses My servant, as I commanded him at Horeb for all Israel, ordinances and judgments.”

units.Leviticus 22:1: And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:
units.Leviticus 22:2: Tell Aaron and his sons to exercise care concerning the holy things of the sons of Israel, which they consecrate to Me, and not profane My holy name. I am the Lord.
units.Leviticus 22:3: Say unto them: Throughout your generations, any man of all your seed who draws near unto the holy things which the sons of Israel consecrate unto the Lord, while his uncleanness is upon him, that soul shall be destroyed from before Me; I am the Lord your God.
units.Leviticus 22:4: And any man among the seed of Aaron the priest who has leprosy or a seminal discharge shall not eat the holy things until he is cleansed. Nor shall one who touches any uncleanness of a person, or a man from whom an emission of semen goes out,
units.Leviticus 22:5: or anyone who touches any unclean creeping creature that defiles him, or a human being who defiles him through any uncleanness of his.
units.Leviticus 22:6: The soul that touches them shall be unclean until evening; he shall not eat of the holy things unless he has bathed his body in water;
units.Leviticus 22:7: and when the sun sets, he shall be clean; afterward he may eat the holy things, for they are his bread.
units.Leviticus 22:8: He shall not eat an animal found dead or torn by beasts, becoming unclean through them. I am the Lord.
units.Leviticus 22:9: And they shall keep My requirements, so that they do not incur sin through them and die through them if they profane them. I am the Lord God who sanctifies them.
units.Leviticus 22:17: And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:
units.Leviticus 22:18: Speak unto Aaron and unto his sons and unto all the congregation of Israel, and you shall say unto them: Any man of the sons of Israel, or of the sons of the resident foreigners attached unto them in Israel, who presents his gifts according to any of their pledges or any of their freewill offerings, which they present unto God for a whole burnt offering,
units.Leviticus 22:19: to be acceptable for you, they shall be males without blemish, from the cattle, the sheep, or the goats.
units.Leviticus 22:20: They shall not bring anything with a blemish unto the Lord, for it will not be acceptable for you.
units.Leviticus 22:21: And if a man presents a sacrifice of deliverance unto the Lord, specifying a vow by voluntary choice or at your feasts, from the cattle or the sheep, it shall be unblemished to be accepted; there shall be no blemish in it.
units.Leviticus 22:22: They shall not bring unto the Lord an animal that is blind, crushed, has its tongue cut, has warts, a severe scab, or skin eruptions. You shall not place any of these on the altar as an offering unto the Lord.
units.Leviticus 22:23: And you may slaughter for yourself a calf or a sheep with a cut-off ear or a shortened tail; but for your vow it shall not be accepted.
units.Leviticus 22:24: You shall not bring unto the Lord an animal castrated by crushing, or by squeezing out, or by cutting out, or by tearing away; and in your land you shall not do this.
units.Leviticus 22:25: And you shall not present any of these as the gifts of your God from the hand of a foreigner, for there are corruptions in them; they have a blemish. These will not be accepted for you.

units.Isaiah 1:12: not even if you come to appear before Me. For who demanded these things from your hands? To trample My court,
units.Isaiah 1:13: you will no longer continue. If you bring fine flour, it is futile. Incense is an abomination to Me. Your new moons and sabbaths and a great day I cannot endure; fasting and idleness,
units.Isaiah 1:14: and your new moons and your festivals My soul hates. You have become more than enough for Me; I will no longer let your sins go.
units.Isaiah 1:15: Whenever you stretch your hands toward Me, I will turn My eyes away from you. Even if you multiply supplication, I will not listen to you, for your hands are full of blood.
units.Isaiah 1:16: Wash yourselves, become clean. Remove the evils from your souls, before My eyes. Stop your evil deeds.

reread_versions.rationale: Malachi appeals to one Creator and Father as the reason not to abandon a brother and profane the covenant. Deuteronomy likewise challenges an unfaithful people by naming the Lord as the Father who acquired, made and created them.
reread_versions.source_text: Did not one God create you? Is there not one Father of you all? Why have you each abandoned your brother, so as to profane the covenant of your fathers?

target_units.text: Do you thus repay the Lord, O foolish people and unwise? Is not He Himself your Father, who acquired you, and made you, and created you?

reread_versions.rationale: Malachi's appeal to one God and one Father grounds responsibility toward a brother. Ephesians similarly names one God and Father of all within its account of the community's unity.
reread_versions.source_text: Did not one God create you? Is there not one Father of you all? Why have you each abandoned your brother, so as to profane the covenant of your fathers?

target_units.text: one God and Father of all, who is over all and through all and in all.

reread_versions.rationale: Malachi charges Judah with profaning the Lord's holy things and devoting himself to foreign gods. Deuteronomy warns against turning away to other gods and contrasts their worship with Israel's identity as God's holy, chosen people.
reread_versions.source_text: Judah has been abandoned, and an abomination has occurred in Israel and Jerusalem, because Judah profaned the Lord’s holy things, in which he delighted, and devoted himself to foreign gods.

target_units.text: For he will turn your son away from Me, and he will serve other gods; and the Lord shall be kindled to wrath against you, and shall destroy you speedily.
But you shall do thus unto them: you shall pull down their altars, and break their pillars, and cut down their sacred groves, and burn the graven images of their gods with fire.
For you are a holy people unto the Lord your God; and the Lord your God has chosen you to be unto Him a people for His own possession, above all the nations upon the face of the earth.

reread_versions.rationale: Malachi threatens removal from Jacob's dwellings after the profanation described in 2:11. Leviticus also announces destruction from among the people for defiling God's holy things; its particular offense of giving offspring to a ruler is distinct from Malachi's wording.
reread_versions.source_text: The Lord will destroy the person who does these things, until he is also humbled away from Jacob’s dwellings and from those who bring a sacrifice to the Lord Almighty.

target_units.text: And I will set My face against that man and destroy him from among his people, because he gave some of his seed to a ruler, defiling My holy things and profaning the name of those consecrated to Me.

reread_versions.rationale: Malachi questions accepting sacrifices despite tears and groaning, with abandonment of a spouse identified in the next verse. Isaiah likewise refuses multiplied prayers from people whose hands carry wrongdoing and requires their conduct to change.
reread_versions.source_text: And you were doing these things that I hated: you covered the Lord’s altar with tears, with weeping and groaning from hardships. Is it still fitting to look toward a sacrifice or accept it from your hands?

target_units.text: Whenever you stretch your hands toward Me, I will turn My eyes away from you. Even if you multiply supplication, I will not listen to you, for your hands are full of blood.
Wash yourselves, become clean. Remove the evils from your souls, before My eyes. Stop your evil deeds.

reread_versions.rationale: Malachi calls the abandoned wife a partner and wife of covenant, with God as witness. Genesis describes the man cleaving to his wife and the two becoming one flesh, grounding the enduring marital bond that abandonment violates.
reread_versions.source_text: And you said, “For what reason?” Because the Lord bore witness between you and the wife of your youth, whom you abandoned, though she is your partner and the wife of your covenant.

target_units.text: And Adam said: This, at last, is bone of my bones and flesh of my flesh. She shall be called Woman, for she was taken from her husband.
For this reason a man shall leave his father and his mother and cleave to his wife, and the two shall become one flesh.

reread_versions.rationale: The closing command of Malachi 2:15 is to guard one's spirit and not abandon the wife of youth. Paul similarly instructs a husband not to dismiss his wife and a wife not to separate, with reconciliation if separation occurs.
reread_versions.source_text: And no other did it, and there was a remnant of his spirit. And you said, “What else does God seek but offspring?” So guard your spirit, and do not abandon the wife of your youth.

target_units.text: To the married I give this instruction—not I, but the Lord: a wife is not to separate from her husband—
but if she does separate, let her remain unmarried or be reconciled to her husband—and a husband is not to dismiss his wife.

reread_versions.rationale: Malachi links sending a hated wife away with impiety and commands against abandonment. Jesus connects divorce with hardness of heart and warns that divorce followed by remarriage, apart from the stated exception, commits adultery.
reread_versions.source_text: But if, after hating her, you send her away, says the Lord, the God of Israel, impiety will cover your thoughts, says the Lord Almighty. So guard your spirit, and you must not abandon.

target_units.text: He said to them, “Because of your hardness of heart Moses permitted you to divorce your wives, but from the beginning it has not been so.
I tell you that whoever divorces his wife, except on account of sexual immorality, and marries another commits adultery.”

reread_versions.rationale: Malachi condemns saying that evildoers are good before God and questioning His righteousness. Isaiah pronounces woe on calling evil good and on justifying the ungodly while denying the righteous their right, indicting the same reversal of moral judgment.
reread_versions.source_text: You who provoke God with your words! And you said, “How have we provoked Him?” By your saying, “Everyone who does evil is good before the Lord, and He has delighted in them,” and, “Where is the God of righteousness?”

target_units.text: Woe to those calling evil good and good evil, making darkness light and light darkness, making bitter sweet and sweet bitter!
Woe to those who are discerning in their own judgment and knowledgeable in their own view!
Woe to your strong ones who drink wine and the powerful who mix strong drink,
who justify the ungodly for gifts and take away the righteous person’s right!

reread_versions.rationale: Malachi announces a messenger attending to a way before the Lord's face. Isaiah calls for preparing the Lord's way before His glory and salvation are revealed, supplying a closely related image of preparation for divine arrival.
reread_versions.source_text: “Look, I am sending out My messenger, and he will look to a way before My face. Suddenly the Lord whom you seek will come to His own sanctuary, and the messenger of the covenant whom you desire. Look, he is coming,” says the Lord Almighty.

target_units.text: A voice of one crying in the wilderness: Prepare the way of the Lord; make straight the paths of our God.
Every valley will be filled, and every mountain and hill will be brought low; all the crooked places will become straight, and the rough country will become plains.
And the glory of the Lord will be seen, and all flesh will see the salvation of God; for the Lord has spoken.

reread_versions.rationale: Jesus identifies John as the prophet about whom the sending of the messenger before the face and preparation of the way was written. The quoted messenger announcement corresponds to Malachi's opening promise, with the quotation's pronouns preserved in Matthew.
reread_versions.source_text: “Look, I am sending out My messenger, and he will look to a way before My face. Suddenly the Lord whom you seek will come to His own sanctuary, and the messenger of the covenant whom you desire. Look, he is coming,” says the Lord Almighty.

target_units.text: But why did you go out? To see a prophet? Yes, I tell you, and more than a prophet.
This is the one about whom it is written: ‘Behold, I send My messenger before Thy face, who will prepare Thy way before Thee.’

reread_versions.rationale: Mark places the messenger-before-the-face announcement beside Isaiah's wilderness voice and then introduces John baptizing. The first announcement corresponds to Malachi's messenger promise, within a combined citation headed by Isaiah in Mark's actual text.
reread_versions.source_text: “Look, I am sending out My messenger, and he will look to a way before My face. Suddenly the Lord whom you seek will come to His own sanctuary, and the messenger of the covenant whom you desire. Look, he is coming,” says the Lord Almighty.

target_units.text: As it is written in Isaiah the prophet: “Look, I send My messenger before Thy face, who will prepare Thy way;
a voice of one crying in the wilderness, ‘Prepare the way of the Lord; make His paths straight.’”
John appeared, baptizing in the wilderness and proclaiming a baptism of repentance for the forgiveness of sins.

reread_versions.rationale: Luke records Jesus identifying John by the written promise of a messenger sent before the face to prepare the way. This repeats Malachi's messenger theme while preserving Luke's wording about preparing the way ahead of the addressed figure.
reread_versions.source_text: “Look, I am sending out My messenger, and he will look to a way before My face. Suddenly the Lord whom you seek will come to His own sanctuary, and the messenger of the covenant whom you desire. Look, he is coming,” says the Lord Almighty.

target_units.text: But what did you go out to see? A prophet? Yes, I tell you, and more than a prophet.
This is the one about whom it is written: ‘Behold, I send My messenger before Thy face, who will prepare Thy way ahead of Thee.’

reread_versions.rationale: Malachi asks who can endure the coming figure's entrance or stand at his appearance. Nahum similarly asks who can stand before the Lord's anger, with melting and crushing imagery emphasizing the overwhelming encounter.
reread_versions.source_text: And who will endure the day of his entrance? Or who will stand at his appearance? For he enters like a smelting fire and like launderers’ herb.

target_units.text: Who will stand before His anger? Who will resist His furious wrath? His fury melts rulers, and rocks were crushed before Him.

reread_versions.rationale: Malachi compares the entrant to a smelting fire. Isaiah describes God's hand bringing a people through burning to purity and removing lawlessness, a corresponding image of divine purification rather than mere outward observance.
reread_versions.source_text: And who will endure the day of his entrance? Or who will stand at his appearance? For he enters like a smelting fire and like launderers’ herb.

target_units.text: I will bring My hand against you and burn you to purity. I will destroy the disobedient, remove all lawless people from you and humble all the arrogant.

reread_versions.rationale: Malachi pictures the sons of Levi cleansed like silver and gold so they can offer rightly. Zechariah likewise describes a remnant refined as silver and tested as gold, followed by restored recognition between God and His people.
reread_versions.source_text: He will sit, smelting and purifying as with silver and gold. He will cleanse the sons of Levi and melt them like gold and silver, and they will be those who bring a sacrifice to the Lord in righteousness.

target_units.text: I will lead the third through fire, refine them with fire as silver is refined and test them as gold is tested. He will call on My name, and I will listen to him and say, ‘This is My people,’ and he will say, ‘The Lord is my God.’”

reread_versions.rationale: Malachi's refiner succeeds in cleansing the priestly sons for righteous sacrifice. Jeremiah describes a silversmith working in vain because wickedness remains, leading to rejected silver; the shared refining image has contrasting outcomes.
reread_versions.source_text: He will sit, smelting and purifying as with silver and gold. He will cleanse the sons of Levi and melt them like gold and silver, and they will be those who bring a sacrifice to the Lord in righteousness.

target_units.text: The bellows failed from the fire; the lead failed. In vain the silversmith works silver; their wickedness was not melted away.
Call them rejected silver, because the Lord rejected them.

reread_versions.rationale: Malachi promises that Judah and Jerusalem's sacrifice will again please the Lord. The psalm asks for Zion's good and Jerusalem's rebuilding, then anticipates God's delight in a sacrifice of righteousness and offerings on His altar.
reread_versions.source_text: And the sacrifice of Judah and Jerusalem will please the Lord, as in the days of old and as in the former years.

target_units.text: Do good to Zion, Lord, in Thy good pleasure, and let Jerusalem’s walls be built.
Then Thou wilt delight in a sacrifice of righteousness, an offering and burnt offerings; then they will bring calves upon Thine altar.

reread_versions.rationale: Malachi's judgment list includes false swearing by God's name and withholding workers' wages. These adjacent Levitical commands prohibit both unjust swearing by God's name and retaining a hired worker's wages overnight.
reread_versions.source_text: “I will draw near to you in judgment, and I will be a swift witness against sorceresses, adulteresses and those who swear falsely by My name, against those who withhold a hired worker’s wages, those who oppress a widow, those who strike orphans with their fists, those who turn aside the judgment of a sojourner, and those who do not fear Me,” says the Lord Almighty.

target_units.text: And you shall not swear by My name for an unjust cause, and you shall not profane the name of your God. I am the Lord your God.
You shall not wrong your neighbour, neither shall you rob; and the wages of the hired worker shall in no wise remain with you overnight until morning.

reread_versions.rationale: Malachi names withheld wages and wrongs against widows, orphans and sojourners. Deuteronomy requires prompt wages for the needy and prohibits perverting judgment for the sojourner, orphan or widow, matching these particular accusations.
reread_versions.source_text: “I will draw near to you in judgment, and I will be a swift witness against sorceresses, adulteresses and those who swear falsely by My name, against those who withhold a hired worker’s wages, those who oppress a widow, those who strike orphans with their fists, those who turn aside the judgment of a sojourner, and those who do not fear Me,” says the Lord Almighty.

target_units.text: You shall not withhold the wages of the poor and needy, whether of your brethren or of the sojourners within your cities.
On the same day you shall pay his wages; the sun shall not go down upon them, for he is poor and sets his hope upon them; lest he cry against you unto the Lord, and there be sin upon you.
Fathers shall not die for children, and sons shall not die for fathers. Each shall die for his own sin.
You shall not pervert the judgment of the sojourner, or of the orphan, or of the widow; neither shall you take a widow’s garment in pledge.

reread_versions.rationale: Malachi promises swift divine testimony against those withholding a hired worker's pay. James says withheld harvest wages cry out and that the harvesters' cries reach the Lord Sabaoth, likewise placing wage injustice before divine judgment.
reread_versions.source_text: “I will draw near to you in judgment, and I will be a swift witness against sorceresses, adulteresses and those who swear falsely by My name, against those who withhold a hired worker’s wages, those who oppress a widow, those who strike orphans with their fists, those who turn aside the judgment of a sojourner, and those who do not fear Me,” says the Lord Almighty.

target_units.text: Look, the wages of the laborers who reaped your fields, withheld by you, cry out; and the cries of the harvesters have entered the ears of the Lord Sabaoth.

reread_versions.rationale: Malachi threatens judgment for harming widows, orphans and sojourners. Exodus prohibits afflicting these groups and says God hears their cries and responds in wrath, supplying the protective principle behind the threatened judgment.
reread_versions.source_text: “I will draw near to you in judgment, and I will be a swift witness against sorceresses, adulteresses and those who swear falsely by My name, against those who withhold a hired worker’s wages, those who oppress a widow, those who strike orphans with their fists, those who turn aside the judgment of a sojourner, and those who do not fear Me,” says the Lord Almighty.

target_units.text: And you shall not ill-treat a resident foreigner, neither shall you afflict him; for you were resident foreigners in the land of Egypt.
You shall not mistreat any widow or orphan.
But if you afflict them, and they cry aloud to Me, I will surely listen to their voice,
I will be angry with wrath and kill you with the sword. Your wives will become widows and your children orphans.

reread_versions.rationale: Malachi's opening declaration says the Lord has not changed. The psalm contrasts changing, perishing creation with God who remains the same and whose years do not fail, expressing the same divine constancy.
reread_versions.source_text: “For I am the Lord your God, and I have not changed. But you, sons of Jacob, do not refrain

target_units.text: They will perish, but Thou wilt remain; all will grow old like a garment. Like a cloak Thou wilt change them, and they will be changed.
But Thou art the same, and Thy years will not fail.

reread_versions.rationale: Malachi declares that the Lord has not changed. James says the Father of lights has no variation or shadow from turning, applying divine constancy to the source of good gifts.
reread_versions.source_text: “For I am the Lord your God, and I have not changed. But you, sons of Jacob, do not refrain

target_units.text: Every good act of giving and every complete gift is from above, coming down from the Father of lights, with whom there is no variation or shadow from turning.

reread_versions.rationale: Both passages give God's invitation, 'Return to Me, and I will return to you,' in the setting of ancestors who departed from His ways. Zechariah's warning against repeating the fathers' practices matches Malachi's indictment of inherited disobedience.
reread_versions.source_text: from the injustices of your fathers. You have turned aside from My ordinances and have not guarded them. Return to Me, and I will return to you,” says the Lord Almighty. And you said, “How shall we return?”

target_units.text: You shall say to them: Thus says the Lord Almighty: Return to Me, and I will return to you, says the Lord.

Do not become like your fathers, against whom the former prophets brought charges, saying, ‘Thus says the Lord Almighty: Turn away from your evil ways and your evil practices.’ But they did not listen attentively to Me, says the Lord.

reread_versions.rationale: Malachi identifies retained tithes and firstfruits as defrauding God. Leviticus declares the land's tithe and the tenth animal holy and belonging to the Lord, explaining why withholding the tithe concerns what is God's.
reread_versions.source_text: “Will a human defraud God? Yet you are defrauding Me.” And you will say, “How have we defrauded Thee?” “Because the tithes and the firstfruits are with you.

target_units.text: Every tithe of the land, from the seed of the land and the fruit of trees, belongs unto the Lord; it is holy unto the Lord.
But if a man indeed redeems his tithe, he shall add a fifth part unto it, and it shall be his.
And every tithe of cattle and sheep, and everything that comes under the staff in the count—the tenth shall be holy unto the Lord.

reread_versions.rationale: Malachi charges the people with withholding dues belonging to God. Numbers assigns Israel's tithes, set apart for the Lord, to the Levites for their service, showing the divinely appointed destination of those dues.
reread_versions.source_text: “Will a human defraud God? Yet you are defrauding Me.” And you will say, “How have we defrauded Thee?” “Because the tithes and the firstfruits are with you.

target_units.text: And to the sons of Levi, look, I have given every tithe in Israel as an allotment in return for their ministries, the service they perform in the Tent of Testimony.
And the sons of Israel shall no longer approach the Tent of Testimony, incurring a death-bringing sin.

And the Levite himself shall perform the ministry of the Tent of Testimony, and they shall bear their offences. It is an everlasting ordinance throughout their generations. Among the sons of Israel they shall receive no inheritance.

For the tithes of the sons of Israel that they set apart for the Lord as a portion set apart I have given to the Levites as an allotment. Therefore I have said to them: Among the sons of Israel they shall receive no allotment.

reread_versions.rationale: Verse 3:9 repeats the charge of defrauding God and adds the nation's disastrous condition. Verse 3:8 identifies the disputed practice as withholding tithes and firstfruits, making the accusation's concrete subject explicit.
reread_versions.source_text: And you keep looking away, yet you are defrauding Me. The nation has been brought to an end.

target_units.text: “Will a human defraud God? Yet you are defrauding Me.” And you will say, “How have we defrauded Thee?” “Because the tithes and the firstfruits are with you.

reread_versions.rationale: Malachi calls for produce dues in the storehouses. Nehemiah recounts Levites deprived of their portions, his rebuke over abandonment of God's house, and the people's subsequent bringing of grain, wine and oil tithes into stores.
reread_versions.source_text: And you brought all the produce dues into the storehouses, and his plunder will be in his house. Examine, then, by this,” says the Lord Almighty, “whether I will not open heaven’s floodgates for you and pour out My blessing for you until there is enough.

target_units.text: I learned that the Levites’ portions had not been given, and the Levites and singers doing the work had fled, each to his field.
I contended with the commanders and said, “Why has God’s house been abandoned?” I gathered them and stationed them at their posts.
All Jouda brought the tithe of wheat, wine and oil into the stores,

into the charge of Selemia the priest, Saddouk the scribe and Phadaia from the Levites, and beside them Anan son of Zakchour, son of Mathania, for they were considered trustworthy; distribution to their brothers rested upon them.

reread_versions.rationale: Malachi promises opening heaven's floodgates and pouring out blessing. Deuteronomy promises that the Lord opens His heavenly treasure to give seasonal rain and bless the people's work, linking heaven's opening with material provision.
reread_versions.source_text: And you brought all the produce dues into the storehouses, and his plunder will be in his house. Examine, then, by this,” says the Lord Almighty, “whether I will not open heaven’s floodgates for you and pour out My blessing for you until there is enough.

target_units.text: The Lord open unto you His good treasure, heaven, to give rain unto your land in its season, and to bless all the works of your hands. And you shall lend unto many nations, but you shall not borrow; and you shall rule over many nations, but they shall not rule over you.

reread_versions.rationale: Malachi promises not to destroy the land's fruit or weaken its vine. Haggai turns attention to formerly fruitless vine and trees and announces blessing from that day, presenting a corresponding reversal toward fruitful land.
reread_versions.source_text: And I will give you instructions for food, and I will certainly not destroy the fruit of your land, and your vine in the field will certainly not grow weak,” says the Lord Almighty.

target_units.text: Please direct your hearts from this day onward; from the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month and from the day the sanctuary of the Lord was founded, put it in your hearts:
whether it will yet be recognized on the threshing floor, and whether the vine, the fig tree, the pomegranate and the olive trees still bear no fruit. From this day I will bless.”

reread_versions.rationale: Malachi says nations will call the people blessed and their land desirable. Deuteronomy describes nations recognizing the Lord's name upon His people alongside multiplied produce and livestock, joining public recognition with blessing in the land.
reread_versions.source_text: “All the nations will call you blessed, because you will be a desirable land,” says the Lord Almighty.

target_units.text: The Lord your God establish you unto Himself a holy people, as He sware unto your fathers, if you hearken unto the voice of the Lord your God, and walk in His ways.
And all the nations of the earth shall see that the name of the Lord is called upon you, and they shall fear you.

And the Lord your God shall multiply you in good things, in the offspring of your womb, and in the produce of your land, and in the offspring of your cattle, upon the land which the Lord sware unto your fathers to give you.

reread_versions.rationale: Both passages accuse the people of provoking God through speech and record their counterquestion asking how they have done so. The renewed disputation introduces the complaint in 3:14-15, following the earlier challenge to divine righteousness in 2:17.
reread_versions.source_text: “You have made your words heavy against Me,” says the Lord. And you said, “How have we spoken against Thee?”

target_units.text: You who provoke God with your words! And you said, “How have we provoked Him?” By your saying, “Everyone who does evil is good before the Lord, and He has delighted in them,” and, “Where is the God of righteousness?”

reread_versions.rationale: Malachi reports the claim that serving God and keeping His observances brings no advantage. The psalmist similarly says he made his heart righteous in vain while enduring daily affliction, voicing the same temptation to regard faithfulness as profitless.
reread_versions.source_text: You said, “The one who serves God is futile. What advantage is there because we guarded His observances and because we walked as supplicants before the Lord Almighty?

target_units.text: And I said, “Then in vain I made my heart righteous and washed my hands among the innocent;
and I became scourged all day, and my rebuke comes in the mornings.”

reread_versions.rationale: Malachi reports that those practicing lawlessness are built up and survive opposition to God. The psalmist envies sinners' peace and describes their arrogant speech and prosperity, giving a fuller account of the same troubling observation.
reread_versions.source_text: And now we call outsiders blessed. All who practice lawlessness are being built up; they opposed God and were saved.”

target_units.text: For I envied the lawless, beholding sinners’ peace,
for there is no refusal at their death, and firmness in their scourging.
They are not in human toils, and they will not be scourged with humans.
Therefore arrogance seized them; they wrapped themselves in their injustice and ungodliness.
Their injustice will come out as though from fat; they passed into a disposition of heart.
They devised and spoke in wickedness; they spoke injustice against the height.
They set their mouth toward heaven, and their tongue passed over the earth.
Therefore my people will return here, and full days will be found for them.
And they said, “How did God know? And is there knowledge in the Most High?”
Behold, these are sinners, and they prosper; for the age they took possession of wealth.

reread_versions.rationale: Malachi says a remembrance book is written before God for those who fear and revere Him. Daniel describes people found inscribed in the book receiving exaltation during affliction; both connect a divine record with favorable recognition, without identifying the books as the same object.
reread_versions.source_text: Those who feared the Lord spoke these things, each to his neighbor. The Lord paid attention and listened, and He wrote a book of remembrance before Him for those who feared the Lord and revered His name.

target_units.text: “At that hour Michael will pass by, the great angel who stands over the sons of your people. That will be a day of affliction such as has not occurred since they came into being until that day. On that day all the people found inscribed in the book will be exalted.

reread_versions.rationale: Malachi's book records those who revere God's name. In Exodus Moses appeals concerning God's written book, and God speaks of blotting out sinners. Both present moral accountability in terms of a book before God, with remembrance and removal as distinct actions.
reread_versions.source_text: Those who feared the Lord spoke these things, each to his neighbor. The Lord paid attention and listened, and He wrote a book of remembrance before Him for those who feared the Lord and revered His name.

target_units.text: Now, if Thou wilt forgive their sin, forgive it; but if not, blot me out of Thy book which Thou hast written.”
The Lord said to Moses, “If anyone has sinned before Me, I will blot him out of My book.

reread_versions.rationale: Malachi says the reverent will belong to God on the day of His acquisition. Exodus promises that those hearing His voice and keeping His covenant will be His treasured people among the nations, expressing the same claim of belonging to God.
reread_versions.source_text: “They will be Mine,” says the Lord Almighty, “for a day that I am making for an acquisition, and I will choose them as a man chooses his son who serves him.

target_units.text: Now therefore, if you diligently listen to My voice, and keep My covenant, you shall be to Me a treasured people from among all the nations; for all the earth is Mine.
And you shall be to Me a royal priesthood and a holy nation.’ These are the words which you shall speak to the sons of Israel.”

reread_versions.rationale: Malachi promises a visible distinction between righteous and lawless people and between serving God and not serving. Matthew portrays final separation in which service or failure to serve the needy is addressed as service or failure toward the King, ending in different outcomes for the righteous and the others.
reread_versions.source_text: And you will return and see the distinction between the righteous and the lawless, and between one who serves God and one who does not serve.

target_units.text: When the Son of Man comes in His glory, and all the angels with Him, then He will sit upon the throne of His glory.
All the nations will be gathered before Him, and He will separate them from one another as the shepherd separates the sheep from the goats.
He will stand the sheep at His right and the young goats at His left.
Then the King will say to those at His right, ‘Come, you blessed by My Father; inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world.
For I was hungry and you gave Me food, I was thirsty and you gave Me drink, I was a stranger and you welcomed Me,
naked and you clothed Me, I was sick and you visited Me, I was in prison and you came to Me.’
Then the righteous will answer Him, ‘Lord, when did we see Thee hungry and feed Thee, or thirsty and give Thee drink?
When did we see Thee a stranger and welcome Thee, or naked and clothe Thee?
When did we see Thee sick or in prison and come to Thee?’
The King will answer them, ‘Truly I tell you, insofar as you did it to one of the least of these My brothers, you did it to Me.’
Then He will also say to those at His left, ‘Depart from Me, you cursed, into the eternal fire prepared for the devil and his angels.
For I was hungry and you did not give Me food, I was thirsty and you did not give Me drink,
I was a stranger and you did not welcome Me, naked and you did not clothe Me, sick and in prison and you did not visit Me.’
Then they too will answer, ‘Lord, when did we see Thee hungry or thirsty or a stranger or naked or sick or in prison, and did not serve Thee?’
Then He will answer them, ‘Truly I tell you, insofar as you did not do it to one of the least of these, neither did you do it to Me.’
And these shall depart into eternal punishment, but the righteous into eternal life.”

reread_versions.rationale: Malachi compares the lawless to straw burned on the coming day, leaving neither root nor branch. Isaiah likewise describes a stalk consumed by flame and roots becoming chaff because the people rejected the Lord's law.
reread_versions.source_text: For look, the day of the Lord is coming, burning like an oven, and it will burn them. All the foreigners and all who practice lawlessness will be straw, and the coming day will ignite them,” says the Lord Almighty, “and neither root nor branch will remain from them.

target_units.text: Therefore, as a stalk is burned by a fiery coal and consumed by a rising flame, their root will become like chaff and their blossom rise like dust. For they did not desire the law of the Lord Sabaoth, but provoked the utterance of the Holy One of Israel.
